title: G-O Hike: Orewa Boardwalk
location: 100 Wellington St, Freemans Bay, Auckland
description:
Hello fellow Get‑Outsiders!

Come join us for a peaceful and refreshing walk around the beautiful Ōrewa Estuary. After introductions, we will follow the Te Ara Tahuna shared path, enjoying the calm water, birdlife, boardwalks, and open green spaces. This is a gentle, scenic outing designed to help us slow down, breathe, and enjoy the natural rhythms of the morning.

We will walk the full estuary loop at a relaxed pace, taking time to appreciate the views and the changing landscape as we circle around the water. After completing the loop, we will finish with a short stroll along Ōrewa Beach together before wrapping up (with possible ice cream).

## **IMPORTANT NOTES & UPDATES:**

• **Car‑pool Meeting Point:** 9.00am at **Nishiki Restaurant, Freemans Bay** (meet in the main carpark area). • **Ōrewa Meeting Point:** 10:00am at the **Ōrewa Surf Lifesaving Club carpark** (on the beachfront). • **Official Route Map:** Auckland Council’s Te Ara Tahuna Estuary Pathway map — `https://www.aucklandcouncil.govt.nz/parks-recreation/get-outdoors/Pages/park-details.aspx?Location=Orewa%20Estuary%20Path` (aucklandcouncil.govt.nz in Bing)

• **Difficulty Rating:** Easy (flat shared path, suitable for most fitness levels). • **Suitability:** Ideal for beginners, returning walkers, and anyone wanting a gentle, scenic outing. • **Completion Time:** We expect to finish by around **2:00pm**. • **Footwear:** Comfortable walking shoes; the path is mostly paved or boardwalk. • **Drinking Water:** Please bring your own. • **Toilets:** Public toilets available near the surf club and along the estuary.

• **RSVP to this event:** Please RSVP “Yes” only if you genuinely intend to come. If your plans change, update your RSVP as soon as possible so others can join. Late cancellations (within 24 hours) or no‑shows may be recorded as such. • **Cellphone Coverage:** Good coverage throughout the walk. • **Transport/Car Pooling:** Please answer the car‑pool question when you RSVP to help with planning.

As I’ve moved into more senior roles in tech, the size and impact of the problems I’ve had to solve have grown significantly. Over time, I realised that the way I was interpreting those challenges was negatively affecting both my mental health and how I showed up at work.

In this short talk, I’ll share how changing the way I interpret problems has helped me become more resilient, learn faster, and perform better—while maintaining my wellbeing. You’ll walk away with a few practical techniques you can apply immediately as a engineer to improve your effectiveness, how you show up, and ultimately help you stand out from your peers.

**A bit about Mark:**

* Mark Pearl is a VP of Engineering at Serko - a business revolutionising business travel. He's a former software engineer, now focused on supporting and leading engineering orgs. He is passionate about helping engineers grow, perform effectively, and show up as good humans. He enjoys sharing practical lessons from his leadership journey to support early-career technologists.

Being part of a Dev Team means working with others, who each have their own way of working and job to do. Successful teams deliver great products because they know how to work effectively together.

title: I Was There!
location: Central City Library, 44-46 Lorne Street, Auckland City Centre, Auckland, Auckland
description:
I Was There! celebrates one man’s deep love of live music in Tāmaki Makaurau. This exhibition brings together original gig posters and handwritten set lists from shows attended between 1990 and 1995 - a golden era for New Zealand music fans.
Featuring legendary acts such as The 3Ds, Straightjacket Fits, Able Tasmans, Tall Dwarfs and many more. Each piece is paired with a short personal reflection that captures what it felt like to be in the room on the night.
Curated by longtime gig‑goer Paul Rowe, who has attended hundreds of shows over his lifetime, the exhibition reflects a time when NZ live music was thriving - played loud and late in iconic venues, some of which have since disappeared.
Step back into the 1990s, relive the sweat, noise and moments that mattered. Bring your own musical memories along and reconnect with the gigs this May.

title: Using Copilot for Design and Actions Workflows
description:
We are back for another edition of the GitHub User Group. This month we dive into using Copilot and AI to enhance the design workflow, and look at how we can leverage AI in our GitHub Actions.

**Product Design with Source Control: Using GitHub, AI, and Preview Builds as Your Source of Truth \~ [Walt Lim](https://www.linkedin.com/in/waltzaround/)**

In this talk, Walt shares how he uses GitHub and AI to rethink the design process, moving beyond traditional prototypes to code as the source of truth. By using pull requests and ephemeral preview builds, he creates fast, realistic, and testable environments where ideas can be reviewed, iterated, and validated in context. Combined with AI-assisted workflows, this approach helps his team move quicker, reduce ambiguity, and make better decisions with less overhead

**From One PR to Another: Agentic Workflows on GitHub \~ [Sinan Nar](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sinannar/)**

A live demo of using AI-driven workflows to trigger actions across repositories—automatically creating a PR in a second repo when changes are merged.
bio: Sinan is an Apps and AI Consultant at ARINCO, a Microsoft and GitHub partner consultancy. He co-organises the Aotearoa Azure User Group and the Auckland .NET User Group. An experienced and certified software engineer, he specialises in the Microsoft ecosystem, with a focus on Azure and GitHub.

**From 5 Days to 5 Minutes: Reimagining QA with Autonomous AI**
In this talk we will go into the detail of not only the launch of the first Well-Architected agents from both AWS and other AWS partners (and what they can and can't do) but will also go through best-practice agentic architecture as verified by AWS senior architects.

Modern software delivery is accelerating faster than traditional QA can keep up. Teams are facing rising costs, delayed releases and significant reputational risks when quality is compromised. At the same time, AI-generated code and rapid release cycles are outpacing manual testing capabilities.

This session explores how autonomous, cloud-native QA powered by AI agents is transforming software verification—reducing testing time from days to minutes and costs from thousands to tens of dollars, supported by AWS Well-Architected principles of:

Operational Excellence: Automating QA workflows with self-service, zero-setup AI agents
Reliability: Detecting broken links, errors and performance issues before production
Cost Optimization: Moving from high fixed QA costs to on-demand, per-run pricing models and more
